answer: A collateral bonding protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock assets in a glacier escrow contract before participating. Each identity stakes capital to generate a certified pearl credential, executing transactions across a vine of mutual credit channels. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of illiquid capital locked per identity. A major limitation is that capital locking penalizes poorer honest agents while failing to deter adversaries with immense liquidity.
